customAnswers.customKey: 1. Build the 'Ready' ranking population filter
customAnswers.value: The Product Owner creates a saved filter in the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira) returning every backlog item in status 'Ready' for the next 2-3 sprints of candidate work. Done when the filter is saved and returns the full ranking population for the planning cycle.

customAnswers.customKey: 1. Verify: Build the 'Ready' ranking population filter
customAnswers.value: Open the saved filter in the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira); pass if it returns only 'Ready' items and the item count matches the board's 'Ready' count for the cycle.

customAnswers.customKey: 2. Populate WSJF inputs on every Ready item
customAnswers.value: The Business Analyst populates the four WSJF input fields (business value, time criticality, risk reduction, job size) or a MoSCoW label on each 'Ready' item in the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira), using the component scores agreed by the team during refinement (Fibonacci relative sizing). Done when 100% of 'Ready' items have all inputs and 0 items lack a job-size estimate.

customAnswers.customKey: 2. Verify: Populate WSJF inputs on every Ready item
customAnswers.value: Run a filter in the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira) for 'Ready' items with any blank WSJF input or missing job size; pass if the result is 0 items.

customAnswers.customKey: 3. Flag incomplete items as 'Needs Refinement'
customAnswers.value: The Product Owner flags any item lacking WSJF inputs as 'Needs Refinement' in the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira) and excludes it from ranking until inputs are complete. Done when every incomplete item carries the flag.

customAnswers.customKey: 3. Verify: Flag incomplete items as 'Needs Refinement'
customAnswers.value: In the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira), list items flagged 'Needs Refinement'; pass if none of them carries a computed rank and no unflagged item is missing inputs.

customAnswers.customKey: 4. Compute and store the WSJF score on each item
customAnswers.value: The Product Owner computes WSJF as (business value + time criticality + risk reduction) / job size for each complete item and stores it in the WSJF custom field in the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira). Done when 100% of 'Ready' items with inputs have a stored score.

customAnswers.customKey: 4. Verify: Compute and store the WSJF score on each item
customAnswers.value: Recompute (value + time-criticality + risk-reduction) / job-size for a sample of ranked items in the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira); pass only if the recomputed score matches the stored score for 100% of sampled items.

customAnswers.customKey: 5. Resolve rank ties in the top 10
customAnswers.value: The Product Owner reviews the ranked order in the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira) and breaks any ties so the ordering is a strict total order with no ties left unresolved among the top 10 items. Done when the top 10 have unique ranks.

customAnswers.customKey: 5. Verify: Resolve rank ties in the top 10
customAnswers.value: Open the ranked backlog in the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira) sorted by WSJF score; pass if no two of the top 10 items share the same rank position.

customAnswers.customKey: 6. Reconcile ranked count to the Ready count
customAnswers.value: The Business Analyst reconciles the count of ranked items against the count of 'Ready' items on the board in the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira) and records the reconciliation on the planning item. Done when the two counts are equal or every gap is a flagged 'Needs Refinement' item.

customAnswers.customKey: 6. Verify: Reconcile ranked count to the Ready count
customAnswers.value: Compare the ranked-item count to the 'Ready' count in the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira); pass if they reconcile exactly, with any delta fully explained by 'Needs Refinement' flags.

customAnswers.customKey: 7. Record rationale for any priority override
customAnswers.value: For any item the Product Owner places out of WSJF order, the Product Owner records the override rationale as a comment on that item in the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira). Done when every override carries a rationale comment.

customAnswers.customKey: 7. Verify: Record rationale for any priority override
customAnswers.value: In the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira), identify items whose position differs from their WSJF-score order; pass if each one has a Product Owner comment stating the override rationale.

customAnswers.customKey: 8. Export the prioritized-order snapshot to the PPM tool
customAnswers.value: The Product Owner exports a timestamped snapshot of the prioritized order for the planning cycle to the PPM tool (Clarity/Planview/Jira Align), preserving the ranking captured in the Jira custom fields with change history. Done once per planning cycle when the snapshot is saved.

customAnswers.customKey: 8. Verify: Export the prioritized-order snapshot to the PPM tool
customAnswers.value: Open the current cycle's snapshot in the PPM tool (Clarity/Planview/Jira Align); pass if it exists, is timestamped for this cycle, and its order matches the ranked backlog in the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira).

customAnswers.customKey: 9. Capture Product Owner sign-off on the ranked backlog
customAnswers.value: The Product Owner records approval of the published ranked backlog (with WSJF scores and the documented method) on the planning item in the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira). Done when the sign-off comment or approval field is recorded.

customAnswers.customKey: 9. Verify: Capture Product Owner sign-off on the ranked backlog
customAnswers.value: Open the planning item in the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira); pass if a Product Owner approval is recorded and dated within the planning cycle.

customAnswers.customKey: 1. Assemble the reviewed-document list in Confluence
customAnswers.value: The Software Engineer compiles the list of reviewed, signed-off documents for the current release (docs-as-code sources, diagrams, API specs) on a Confluence page, sourcing content only from the reviewed, signed-off versions. Done when the list covers the full release documentation set with each document's review reference.

customAnswers.customKey: 1. Verify: Assemble the reviewed-document list in Confluence
customAnswers.value: Open the release documentation list page in Confluence; pass if every document in the release set is listed and each row links to its review sign-off.

customAnswers.customKey: 2. Raise a pull request committing the documents
customAnswers.value: The Software Engineer commits every reviewed document to the docs area of the source code/CI-CD repository via a pull request, never by direct commit to main. Done when the PR contains all documents from the reviewed list.

customAnswers.customKey: 2. Verify: Raise a pull request committing the documents
customAnswers.value: Open the PR in the source code/CI-CD repository; pass if it contains the committed documents, targets main via PR (no direct commits), and the committed content matches the approved review artifacts.

customAnswers.customKey: 3. Link the PR to the release change ticket
customAnswers.value: The Software Engineer adds the release change ticket / work item reference to the PR description in the source code/CI-CD repository. Done when the link resolves to the correct ticket.

customAnswers.customKey: 3. Verify: Link the PR to the release change ticket
customAnswers.value: Open the PR description in the source code/CI-CD repository; pass if it contains a working link to the release change ticket / work item.

customAnswers.customKey: 4. Record intentional exclusions in the PR description
customAnswers.value: The Software Engineer lists any document intentionally excluded from version control in the PR description in the source code/CI-CD repository, each with its reason (e.g. superseded) and disposition. Done when every excluded document is logged.

customAnswers.customKey: 4. Verify: Record intentional exclusions in the PR description
customAnswers.value: Compare the reviewed-document list against the PR contents in the source code/CI-CD repository; pass if every document absent from the PR appears in the exclusion list with a reason.

customAnswers.customKey: 5. Obtain an approving review on the documentation PR
customAnswers.value: The Backend Developer (or UI Developer) reviews the documentation PR in the source code/CI-CD repository and records an approving review. Done when at least one approval from a reviewer other than the author is present.

customAnswers.customKey: 5. Verify: Obtain an approving review on the documentation PR
customAnswers.value: Open the PR in the source code/CI-CD repository; pass if it shows at least one approving review from someone other than the PR author.

customAnswers.customKey: 6. Confirm the CI docs build is green
customAnswers.value: The Software Engineer confirms the CI docs-build check on the PR in the source code/CI-CD repository passes before merge. Done when the docs-build status is green on the head commit.

customAnswers.customKey: 6. Verify: Confirm the CI docs build is green
customAnswers.value: Open the CI checks on the PR in the source code/CI-CD repository; pass if the docs-build run for the merge commit is green.

customAnswers.customKey: 7. Merge and tag the documentation to the release
customAnswers.value: The Software Engineer merges the PR and applies the release version tag in the source code/CI-CD repository, recording commit SHA and UTC timestamp; prior versions remain retrievable in git history. Done when the tag points at the merge commit.

customAnswers.customKey: 7. Verify: Merge and tag the documentation to the release
customAnswers.value: Open the tag in the source code/CI-CD repository; pass if it points at the merged documentation commit, the SHA and timestamp are recorded, and a prior document version can be retrieved from history.

customAnswers.customKey: 8. Reconcile the review list against the repo tree
customAnswers.value: The Software Engineer reconciles the reviewed-document list from Confluence against the merged repo tree in the source code/CI-CD repository: count reviewed must equal count committed with 0 gaps, and the diff must show only intended changes. Done when the reconciliation is recorded on the PR.

customAnswers.customKey: 8. Verify: Reconcile the review list against the repo tree
customAnswers.value: Compare the Confluence reviewed list to the repository tree in the source code/CI-CD repository; pass if every reviewed document is present at the expected version and the reconciliation note shows 0 gaps.

customAnswers.customKey: 1. Build the eligible-item list at iteration close
customAnswers.value: The Business Analyst runs a filter in the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira) for all backlog items in status Done or De-scoped/Won't-Do at sprint/PI close, within 2 business days of iteration close. Done when the eligible list and its count are recorded on the archival ticket.

customAnswers.customKey: 1. Verify: Build the eligible-item list at iteration close
customAnswers.value: Open the saved filter and archival ticket in the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira); pass if the list covers only Done and De-scoped items at close and the run date is within 2 business days of iteration close.

customAnswers.customKey: 2. Verify closure metadata on each eligible item
customAnswers.value: The Business Analyst checks each eligible item in the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira) for final status, closure rationale, resolver, closure date, and a link to the delivering PR/release (for Done) or the de-scope decision record (for de-scoped). Done when every item is either complete or held back.

customAnswers.customKey: 2. Verify: Verify closure metadata on each eligible item
customAnswers.value: Inspect the archived items in the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira); pass if 100% carry final status, rationale, resolver, closure date, and the required delivery or de-scope link.

customAnswers.customKey: 3. Raise sub-tasks for items missing closure rationale
customAnswers.value: For any item flagged Done/de-scoped but missing rationale, the Product Owner holds it back from archival and creates a 'closure-rationale-missing' sub-task in the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira) assigned to the item owner, to be resolved within 3 business days. Done when every held-back item has such a sub-task.

customAnswers.customKey: 3. Verify: Raise sub-tasks for items missing closure rationale
customAnswers.value: In the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira), list held-back items; pass if each has a 'closure-rationale-missing' sub-task with an owner and a due date within 3 business days.

customAnswers.customKey: 4. Tag audit-relevant items for 7-year retention
customAnswers.value: The Product Owner tags items linked to regulatory or audit deliverables in the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira) for 7-year retention per the enterprise records-retention policy and internal SOX/records policy; ordinary items follow the 12-month operational retention. Done when every audit-relevant item carries the retention tag.

customAnswers.customKey: 4. Verify: Tag audit-relevant items for 7-year retention
customAnswers.value: Filter archived items linked to regulatory/audit deliverables in the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira); pass if each carries the 7-year retention tag and cites the records-retention policy.

customAnswers.customKey: 5. Move eligible items to the archived board
customAnswers.value: The Product Owner moves all eligible, metadata-complete items to the archived project/board in the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira), stamped with iteration ID and UTC timestamp, preserving full history (transitions, comments, links); archival is reversible for 30 days. Done when no eligible item remains on the active backlog.

customAnswers.customKey: 5. Verify: Move eligible items to the archived board
customAnswers.value: Open the archived board in the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira); pass if the items are present with full history and iteration ID, a sampled item is restorable, and the active backlog contains no remaining eligible items.

customAnswers.customKey: 6. Reconcile eligible count to archived count
customAnswers.value: The Business Analyst reconciles the count of eligible items (Done + De-scoped at close) against the count archived in the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira); the delta must be 0 excluding held-back items. Done when the reconciliation result is recorded on the archival ticket.

customAnswers.customKey: 6. Verify: Reconcile eligible count to archived count
customAnswers.value: Compare the eligible-list count to the archived-board count in the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira); pass if the delta is 0 with any difference fully explained by held-back sub-tasks.

customAnswers.customKey: 7. Attach the archival export snapshot
customAnswers.value: The Business Analyst exports a snapshot of the archived items and attaches it to the archival ticket in the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira) with the iteration ID and UTC timestamp. Done when the snapshot attachment is present.

customAnswers.customKey: 7. Verify: Attach the archival export snapshot
customAnswers.value: Open the archival ticket in the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira); pass if the export snapshot is attached, timestamped, and its row count equals the archived count.

customAnswers.customKey: 8. Capture Product Owner sign-off on the archival run
customAnswers.value: The Product Owner reviews the reconciliation and exceptions and records approval of the archival run on the archival ticket in the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira). Done when the approval is recorded within 2 business days of iteration close.

customAnswers.customKey: 8. Verify: Capture Product Owner sign-off on the archival run
customAnswers.value: Open the archival ticket in the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira); pass if a dated Product Owner approval is recorded and the run completed within the 2-business-day SLA.

customAnswers.customKey: 1. Compile the release governance artefact list
customAnswers.value: The Software Engineer compiles the list of governance artefacts for services deployed to production this release: architecture review record, ADRs, security review sign-off, threat model, test evidence, and change approval — typically 4-8 evidence items per service, one per governance gate (arch, security, test, change). Done when every gate has at least one artefact listed.

customAnswers.customKey: 1. Verify: Compile the release governance artefact list
customAnswers.value: Compare the compiled list against the release governance checklist; pass if all four gate types are covered for every deployed service with at least one evidence item each.

customAnswers.customKey: 2. Upload each artefact to the compliance evidence repository
customAnswers.value: The Software Engineer uploads every listed artefact to the compliance evidence repository within 5 business days of production go-live. Done when all artefacts on the list are present in the repository.

customAnswers.customKey: 2. Verify: Upload each artefact to the compliance evidence repository
customAnswers.value: Open the release folder in the compliance evidence repository; pass if every artefact from the list is present and the upload dates are within 5 business days of go-live.

customAnswers.customKey: 3. Tag each artefact with the required index metadata
customAnswers.value: The Software Engineer tags each artefact's index entry in the compliance evidence repository with release ID, change ticket number, artefact type, approver, and date. Done when all five fields are populated on every entry.

customAnswers.customKey: 3. Verify: Tag each artefact with the required index metadata
customAnswers.value: Inspect the index entries in the compliance evidence repository; pass if release ID, change ticket, artefact type, approver, and date are populated on 100% of entries.

customAnswers.customKey: 4. Record immutable version, hash, and timestamp
customAnswers.value: The Software Engineer records the immutable version, SHA-256 hash, and UTC timestamp on each artefact in the compliance evidence repository, with the index entry referencing the source change ticket and release SHA. Done when every artefact has a hash and timestamp.

customAnswers.customKey: 4. Verify: Record immutable version, hash, and timestamp
customAnswers.value: Recompute the SHA-256 hash of a sampled artefact in the compliance evidence repository; pass if it matches the recorded hash and the entry shows the UTC timestamp and release SHA.

customAnswers.customKey: 5. Apply the 'SDLC-7Y' retention policy
customAnswers.value: The Software Engineer applies the 7-year retention policy 'SDLC-7Y' to the release folder in the compliance evidence repository, with auto-purge disabled until retention elapses and the legal-hold flag respected. Done when the retention class shows SDLC-7Y on all entries.

customAnswers.customKey: 5. Verify: Apply the 'SDLC-7Y' retention policy
customAnswers.value: Open the retention settings on the release folder in the compliance evidence repository; pass if retention class is 'SDLC-7Y', auto-purge is disabled, and legal-hold handling is enabled.

customAnswers.customKey: 6. Cite the regulatory and policy references on the index
customAnswers.value: The Software Engineer records NYDFS 23 NYCRR 500.06 (audit trail), 500.14, and the internal SDLC-GOV-01 records-retention standard on the archive index entry in the compliance evidence repository. Done when the citations appear on the release index entry.

customAnswers.customKey: 6. Verify: Cite the regulatory and policy references on the index
customAnswers.value: Open the release index entry in the compliance evidence repository; pass if it cites NYDFS 500.06, 500.14, and SDLC-GOV-01.

customAnswers.customKey: 7. Reconcile archived artefacts to the governance checklist
customAnswers.value: The Tech Lead compares the pre-archive governance checklist against the post-archive index in the compliance evidence repository: artefact count must equal the checklist item count with 0 missing gates and matching hashes. Done when the comparison result shows a 0 delta.

customAnswers.customKey: 7. Verify: Reconcile archived artefacts to the governance checklist
customAnswers.value: Compare index count to governance-checklist count for the release in the compliance evidence repository; pass only if the delta is 0 and all hashes match the pre-archive values.

customAnswers.customKey: 8. Log any missing or unapproved artefact as an exception
customAnswers.value: The Tech Lead logs each missing or unapproved artefact as an exception with owner and disposition of obtained-and-archived or risk-accepted-with-sign-off, under a 10-business-day remediation SLA; missing evidence blocks release closure. Done when every reconciliation gap has a logged exception.

customAnswers.customKey: 8. Verify: Log any missing or unapproved artefact as an exception
customAnswers.value: For each gap found in reconciliation, open the exception record; pass if it names an owner, a disposition, and a remediation date within 10 business days.

customAnswers.customKey: 9. Capture Tech Lead sign-off on the completed archive
customAnswers.value: The Tech Lead records approval that the archive is complete on the release index entry in the compliance evidence repository. Done when the sign-off with approver and date is recorded.

customAnswers.customKey: 9. Verify: Capture Tech Lead sign-off on the completed archive
customAnswers.value: Open the release index entry in the compliance evidence repository; pass if a dated Tech Lead approval is recorded after the reconciliation shows 0 missing gates.

customAnswers.customKey: 1. Generate the quarterly archival worklist
customAnswers.value: The Software Engineer queries the Confluence 'Engineering Knowledge Base' space in the first business week of the quarter for pages whose 'Last reviewed' label is older than 12 months (last modified on or before the rolling 12-month cutoff) or whose subject component is decommissioned, excluding regulatory/actuarial governance docs held in the model governance repository. Done when the worklist with page IDs is exported.

customAnswers.customKey: 1. Verify: Generate the quarterly archival worklist
customAnswers.value: Open the archival worklist; pass if it was produced in the first business week of the quarter, lists page IDs, and every row meets the older-than-12-months or decommissioned-component criterion.

customAnswers.customKey: 2. Confirm a replacement reference for every page
customAnswers.value: The Software Engineer confirms each worklist page has a link to the current replacement page or a 'No replacement - capability retired, CMDB CI xxxxx' note; pages missing a replacement reference are blocked from archival. Done when every row carries a replacement URL or retirement note.

customAnswers.customKey: 2. Verify: Confirm a replacement reference for every page
customAnswers.value: Scan the worklist; pass if 0 rows lack a replacement URL or a retirement note with the CMDB CI reference.

customAnswers.customKey: 3. Apply the Archived banner and sunset date in Confluence
customAnswers.value: The Software Engineer adds a 'Status: Archived' banner, records the sunset date in the Confluence 'Sunset' page property, and adds the replacement link on each page in Confluence. Done when every archived page carries all three.

customAnswers.customKey: 3. Verify: Apply the Archived banner and sunset date in Confluence
customAnswers.value: Sample 25 archived pages in Confluence; pass only if 100% show the Archived banner, a sunset date in the 'Sunset' property, and a valid (resolving) replacement link.

customAnswers.customKey: 4. Move archived pages to the Confluence Archive space
customAnswers.value: The Software Engineer moves each processed page to the 'Archive' space in Confluence, preserving page-version history. Done when all non-deferred worklist pages are in the Archive space.

customAnswers.customKey: 4. Verify: Move archived pages to the Confluence Archive space
customAnswers.value: Open the Archive space in Confluence; pass if the moved pages are present with intact version history and no processed page remains in the Engineering Knowledge Base space.

customAnswers.customKey: 5. Mark superseded READMEs in the platform repos
customAnswers.value: The Software Engineer updates superseded READMEs in the 'platform-*' repos in the source code/CI-CD repository via commit, marking each as archived with a sunset date and a pointer to the replacement documentation. Done when every superseded README on the worklist is updated.

customAnswers.customKey: 5. Verify: Mark superseded READMEs in the platform repos
customAnswers.value: Open the commits in the source code/CI-CD repository; pass if each superseded README shows the archived marking, sunset date, and replacement pointer.

customAnswers.customKey: 6. Log deferred pages with reason and SLA
customAnswers.value: The Software Engineer logs any page that cannot be archived (still linked from a live runbook, no owner, or replacement not yet published) with disposition 'Deferred - reason' and a 10-business-day resolution SLA. Done when every unarchived worklist row has a deferral record.

customAnswers.customKey: 6. Verify: Log deferred pages with reason and SLA
customAnswers.value: Compare the worklist to the archived set; pass if every unarchived row has a deferral record stating the reason, owner, and a resolution date within 10 business days.

customAnswers.customKey: 7. Reconcile archived count to the worklist
customAnswers.value: The Software Engineer reconciles the count of pages moved to the Confluence Archive space against the worklist count; the delta must be 0 (net of logged deferrals) before the run is marked complete, with no net loss of content — only status transitions. Done when the reconciliation is recorded.

customAnswers.customKey: 7. Verify: Reconcile archived count to the worklist
customAnswers.value: Compare Archive-space additions to the worklist in Confluence; pass if archived + deferred = worklist total with delta 0 and total live+archived page count shows no content loss.

customAnswers.customKey: 8. Sweep for stale pages still tagged current
customAnswers.value: The Software Engineer runs a full sweep of the Engineering Knowledge Base space in Confluence for any page still tagged 'current' whose 'Last reviewed' label is more than 12 months old. Done when the sweep returns 0 stale current pages.

customAnswers.customKey: 8. Verify: Sweep for stale pages still tagged current
customAnswers.value: Run the stale-page query in Confluence; pass only if 0 pages tagged 'current' have a last-reviewed date older than 12 months.

customAnswers.customKey: 9. Attach the archival worklist CSV and close the run
customAnswers.value: The Software Engineer attaches the archival worklist CSV (page ID, sunset date, replacement URL, archiver, ISO-8601 timestamp) to the quarterly run page in Confluence, retained 3 years, and records run completion. Done when the CSV is attached and the run is marked complete.

customAnswers.customKey: 9. Verify: Attach the archival worklist CSV and close the run
customAnswers.value: Open the quarterly run page in Confluence; pass if the CSV is attached with all five columns populated, an ISO-8601 timestamp, and a completion note by the Software Engineer.

customAnswers.customKey: 1. Confirm the epic's architecture context in Jira
customAnswers.value: The Software Engineer opens the candidate epic in the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira) and confirms its architecture context names the affected systems (Guidewire policy/claims/billing, integration layer, data platform), during discovery 1-2 sprints before the epic enters a sprint. Done when the context section is complete.

customAnswers.customKey: 1. Verify: Confirm the epic's architecture context in Jira
customAnswers.value: Open the epic in the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira); pass if the architecture context lists the affected systems and the epic has not yet entered a sprint.

customAnswers.customKey: 2. Run a feasibility spike in the repository
customAnswers.value: The Backend Developer and UI Developer run a feasibility spike on a branch in the source code/CI-CD repository to probe the risky integration points identified in the epic. Done when the spike branch exists and is linked to the epic.

customAnswers.customKey: 2. Verify: Run a feasibility spike in the repository
customAnswers.value: Open the spike branch/PR in the source code/CI-CD repository; pass if it exists, references the epic key, and contains the spike work.

customAnswers.customKey: 3. Document the feasibility record on the epic
customAnswers.value: The Software Engineer records on the epic in the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira): affected systems/CMDB CIs, integration points, estimated complexity (T-shirt or story-point range using the approved reference-class story pointing + risk-adjusted T-shirt sizing method), key technical risks, and required non-functional constraints. Done when no field is left as TBD.

customAnswers.customKey: 3. Verify: Document the feasibility record on the epic
customAnswers.value: Open the feasibility record on the epic in the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira); pass if all mandatory sections are populated, the methodology version is noted, and 0 fields read TBD.

customAnswers.customKey: 4. Reconcile named systems to CMDB CIs
customAnswers.value: The Business Analyst reconciles every dependency/system named in the feasibility record to a CMDB CI or a documented external service, recording the links on the epic in the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira). Done when the count of named systems equals the count of linked CIs.

customAnswers.customKey: 4. Verify: Reconcile named systems to CMDB CIs
customAnswers.value: Count the systems named in the feasibility record and the linked CIs in the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira); pass only if the counts are equal with no unlinked dependency.

customAnswers.customKey: 5. Apply the estimate-sensitivity check
customAnswers.value: The Software Engineer computes best-case and worst-case effort on the epic in the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira); if the estimate varies by more than 30%, the epic is flagged high-uncertainty and requires a de-risking spike before commitment. Done when the variance and any flag are recorded.

customAnswers.customKey: 5. Verify: Apply the estimate-sensitivity check
customAnswers.value: Open the feasibility record in the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira); pass if best/worst-case variance is recorded and, where it exceeds 30%, the high-uncertainty flag and de-risking spike requirement are present.

customAnswers.customKey: 6. Log open technical risks as Jira risk items
customAnswers.value: The Software Engineer logs each open technical risk from the feasibility record as a risk item in the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira) with an owner and mitigation; a 'not feasible as scoped' finding routes back to re-scoping via a documented decision. Done when every risk in the record has a risk item.

customAnswers.customKey: 6. Verify: Log open technical risks as Jira risk items
customAnswers.value: Cross-check risks in the feasibility record against risk items in the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira); pass if each risk has an item with owner and mitigation populated.

customAnswers.customKey: 7. Attach the versioned ADR and spike report to the epic
customAnswers.value: The Software Engineer attaches the ADR and spike report to the epic in the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira), versioned with author and date, retained for the life of the initiative. Done when both artefacts are attached.

customAnswers.customKey: 7. Verify: Attach the versioned ADR and spike report to the epic
customAnswers.value: Open the epic attachments in the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira); pass if the ADR and spike report are present with author and date recorded.

customAnswers.customKey: 8. Record the feasibility verdict and review flag
customAnswers.value: The Software Engineer records the verdict (feasible / feasible-with-conditions / not-feasible) with complexity range, risk list, and dependency map on the epic in the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira); epics estimated above 20 story points or touching 2 or more core systems are flagged for formal architecture review before build. Done when the verdict and any review flag are recorded.

customAnswers.customKey: 8. Verify: Record the feasibility verdict and review flag
customAnswers.value: Open the epic in the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira); pass if the verdict field is populated, the materiality flag is present where the 20-point or 2-core-system threshold is met, and the record shows the reviewer's sign-off; an epic proceeding to build without it must show an 'SDLC-Exception' ticket.

customAnswers.customKey: 1. Pull the unassigned intake queue
customAnswers.value: The Demand Manager runs the intake filter in the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira) for every request in status 'New/Triaged' that lacks an accountable product owner or engineering team, at each triage cycle (daily/weekly per team cadence). Done when the queue for the cycle is listed.

customAnswers.customKey: 1. Verify: Pull the unassigned intake queue

customAnswers.customKey: 2. Verify: Populate the mandatory gate-record fields

customAnswers.customKey: 2. Apply the required tag set to each article in Confluence
customAnswers.value: The Backend Developer and UI Developer tag each in-scope article in Confluence with domain/value-stream, component (from the CMDB), lifecycle status, and owner, using only labels from the controlled taxonomy (no free-text labels); every article needs at least 3 required tags. Done when 100% of in-scope articles are tagged.

customAnswers.customKey: 2. Verify: Apply the required tag set to each article in Confluence
customAnswers.value: Sample tagged articles in Confluence; pass if each carries >=3 required tags drawn from the controlled taxonomy and no free-text labels appear.

customAnswers.customKey: 3. Raise KM-hygiene tickets for untaggable articles in the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira)
customAnswers.value: The Software Engineer logs a 'KM-hygiene' ticket in the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira) for each article that cannot be tagged (obsolete/ambiguous), owned by the article's team lead with a disposition of archive/rewrite/keep and a 10-business-day disposition SLA; unresolved items escalate to the knowledge-management owner. Done when every untaggable article is ticketed.

customAnswers.customKey: 3. Verify: Raise KM-hygiene tickets for untaggable articles in the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira)
customAnswers.value: List 'KM-hygiene' tickets in the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira); pass if every untaggable article is referenced in a ticket with owner, disposition options, and SLA date.

customAnswers.customKey: 4. Reconcile tagging counts against the audit total
customAnswers.value: The Software Engineer reconciles: tagged articles + explicitly archived articles = total in-scope from the audit query, with 0 unaccounted, and the label taxonomy report shows no orphan labels. Done when the reconciliation balances.

customAnswers.customKey: 4. Verify: Reconcile tagging counts against the audit total
customAnswers.value: Compare the tag counts to the audit export; pass if tagged plus archived equals the in-scope total with 0 unaccounted and the taxonomy report lists no orphan labels.

customAnswers.customKey: 5. Verify search discoverability by tag facet in Confluence
customAnswers.value: The UI Developer runs a search on each required tag facet in Confluence and confirms it returns the expected article set. Done when every facet search resolves correctly.

customAnswers.customKey: 5. Verify: Verify search discoverability by tag facet in Confluence
customAnswers.value: Execute a search per required tag facet in Confluence; pass if each returns the expected article set for that facet.

customAnswers.customKey: 6. Save the tagging evidence in Confluence
customAnswers.value: The Software Engineer saves the Confluence label report and the quarterly audit query export in the Engineering space; page history retains each label change with user and timestamp. Done when both artifacts are stored.

customAnswers.customKey: 6. Verify: Save the tagging evidence in Confluence

customAnswers.value: The Software Engineer re-runs the audit query in Confluence to confirm 0 untagged in-scope articles remain, then records the Tech Lead's approval on the quarterly tagging record. Done when the query returns zero and the sign-off is recorded.

customAnswers.customKey: 7. Verify: Re-run the audit and record Tech Lead sign-off in Confluence
customAnswers.value: Re-run the audit query in Confluence; pass if it returns 0 untagged in-scope articles and the tagging record shows Tech Lead approval with date.

customAnswers.value: The Integration Engineer reconciles the verified contracts in Pact Broker against the service dependency map so every declared integration has a contract, with 0 dependencies uncovered. Done when the reconciliation shows no gaps.

customAnswers.customKey: 4. Verify: Reconcile broker contracts against the dependency map
customAnswers.value: Compare the Pact Broker contract list to the dependency map; pass if every declared integration has a corresponding contract and the uncovered count is 0.

customAnswers.customKey: 5. Classify contract changes and process breaking changes
customAnswers.value: The Software Engineer classifies changes per the sensitivity rule — any change to the required field set or a type is breaking and triggers a version bump; optional-field additions are non-breaking — and logs each required breaking change as an 'SDLC-Exception' (owner = Integration Architect) with consumer notification, consumer sign-off, and a migration window. Done when no breaking change ships without a versioned contract and sign-off.

customAnswers.customKey: 5. Verify: Classify contract changes and process breaking changes
customAnswers.value: Review changed contracts; pass if every required-set/type change has a version bump, an 'SDLC-Exception' ticket owned by the Integration Architect, and recorded consumer sign-off.

customAnswers.customKey: 6. Re-run stale verifications in Pact Broker
customAnswers.value: The Integration Engineer re-runs any verification in Pact Broker whose timestamp is older than the release candidate, so every pair is 'verified' within the RC freeze-to-sign-off window; a contract must be verified for its provider+consumer version pair before deploy. Done when no stale verifications remain.

customAnswers.customKey: 6. Verify: Re-run stale verifications in Pact Broker
customAnswers.value: Check verification timestamps in Pact Broker; pass if every pair's verification is newer than the RC build and status is 'verified'.

customAnswers.customKey: 7. Confirm the release gate and record Integration Architect sign-off
customAnswers.value: The Software Engineer confirms 100% of contract pairs are green in Pact Broker at the release gate, archives the SHA-keyed CI logs in the source code/CI-CD repository (retained 400 days), and records the Integration Architect's approval. Done when the gate report is all green and signed.

customAnswers.customKey: 7. Verify: Confirm the release gate and record Integration Architect sign-off
customAnswers.value: Open the release gate record; pass if all pairs are green in Pact Broker, the CI logs are archived keyed to the commit SHA, and Integration Architect approval is recorded.

customAnswers.customKey: 1. Pull the Ready-for-Review story set from the requirements repository
customAnswers.value: The Business Analyst pulls all elaborated stories at status 'Ready for Review' for the current epic from the requirements repository (excluding 'Draft' and 'Backlog'), typically 15-40 stories per sprint within the active PI window. Done when the review set and its count are recorded.

customAnswers.customKey: 1. Verify: Pull the Ready-for-Review story set from the requirements repository
customAnswers.value: Run the Ready-for-Review query in the requirements repository; pass if the result matches the epic's linked stories excluding Draft/Backlog and the count is recorded.

customAnswers.customKey: 2. Pre-check required fields on each story in the requirements repository
customAnswers.value: The Business Analyst pre-checks that each story has non-empty Gherkin Given/When/Then acceptance criteria, a testable definition of done, and a linked business owner in the requirements repository; required-field automation blocks the transition to 'Validated' if any field is empty. Done when every story passes the field check before the session.

customAnswers.customKey: 2. Verify: Pre-check required fields on each story in the requirements repository
customAnswers.value: Inspect each story in the requirements repository; pass if AC, DoD, and business-owner link are populated and no story bypassed the Validated-transition block.

customAnswers.customKey: 3. Flag material stories touching regulated flows in the requirements repository
customAnswers.value: The Business Analyst flags stories affecting regulated flows (rating, claims payout, PII handling) as 'material' in the requirements repository; material stories require compliance reviewer sign-off before build. Done when every regulated-flow story carries the flag.

customAnswers.customKey: 3. Verify: Flag material stories touching regulated flows in the requirements repository
customAnswers.value: Filter material-flagged stories in the requirements repository; pass if every story touching rating, claims payout, or PII is flagged and tracks a compliance sign-off requirement.

customAnswers.customKey: 4. Hold the stakeholder validation session
customAnswers.value: The Business Analyst holds the validation session with the business stakeholders and the Product Owner, following BABOK v3 elicitation methods per the BA Playbook v2.1, with the method version recorded on each story. Done when the session covers all Ready-for-Review stories.

customAnswers.customKey: 4. Verify: Hold the stakeholder validation session
customAnswers.value: Open the session record; pass if it covers the full story set and each story records the BABOK v3 / BA Playbook v2.1 method version.

customAnswers.customKey: 5. Disposition every story in the review log in the requirements repository
customAnswers.value: The Business Analyst records a disposition (Accepted / Changed / Rejected) for every reviewed story in the requirements repository review log, with 0 stories left un-dispositioned at session close; any acceptance-criteria change affecting more than 20% of a story's scope triggers mandatory re-validation with the business owner. Done when reviewed count equals dispositioned count.

customAnswers.customKey: 5. Verify: Disposition every story in the review log in the requirements repository
customAnswers.value: Open the review log in the requirements repository; pass if stories reviewed equals stories dispositioned, and >20%-scope changes carry a re-validation flag.

customAnswers.customKey: 6. Raise Requirement-Clarification sub-tasks for disputes in the requirements repository
customAnswers.value: The Business Analyst raises a 'Requirement-Clarification' sub-task in the requirements repository for every disputed requirement, with disposition (accepted/rework/deferred), assignee, and a due date within 5 business days; failed stories move to 'Needs Rework' and breaches escalate to the Product Owner. Done when every dispute is ticketed.

customAnswers.customKey: 6. Verify: Raise Requirement-Clarification sub-tasks for disputes in the requirements repository
customAnswers.value: List 'Requirement-Clarification' sub-tasks in the requirements repository; pass if every disputed requirement has one with disposition, assignee, and a due date within 5 business days.

customAnswers.customKey: 7. Publish the signed validation minutes
customAnswers.value: The Business Analyst publishes the signed validation minutes with per-story feedback under the epic space using the filename '<EPIC>-requirements-validation-vN', versioned and timestamped with attachments retained 3 years, and notifies the distribution list: product owner, assigned engineers, business owner, and scrum master. Done when the minutes and notifications exist.

customAnswers.customKey: 7. Verify: Publish the signed validation minutes
customAnswers.value: Open the minutes page; pass if it follows the '<EPIC>-requirements-validation-vN' naming with version/timestamp and the notification to the four-role distribution list is recorded.

customAnswers.customKey: 8. Record Product Owner approval on the epic in the requirements repository
customAnswers.value: The Product Owner records the validation decision (approved/rework) on the epic's Validation field in the requirements repository with reviewer, date, and a link to the minutes; approval authority follows the governance RACI, with delegation to the Business Analyst allowed only for non-material stories and recorded in the delegation table. Done when the Validation field is set, targeting at least 95% first-pass approval.

customAnswers.customKey: 8. Verify: Record Product Owner approval on the epic in the requirements repository
customAnswers.value: Open the epic in the requirements repository; pass if the Validation field shows the decision with reviewer, date, and minutes link, delegation (if any) is limited to non-material stories, and the first-pass approval rate is measured against the 95% target.

customAnswers.customKey: 1. Enumerate changed code paths in the source code/CI-CD repository
customAnswers.value: The Software Engineer enumerates every changed public method and branch in the pull request diff in the source code/CI-CD repository as the test population. Done when the list of changed paths requiring tests is complete.

customAnswers.customKey: 1. Verify: Enumerate changed code paths in the source code/CI-CD repository
customAnswers.value: Review the PR diff in the source code/CI-CD repository; pass if every changed public method and branch is identified in the test population with none omitted.

customAnswers.customKey: 2. Author unit tests for each changed path in the source code/CI-CD repository
customAnswers.value: The Backend Developer and UI Developer author unit tests for their changed paths in the source code/CI-CD repository: each test uses clear arrange/act/assert, a meaningful name, asserts behavior not implementation, and is deterministic (no reliance on wall-clock or network); no changed public method is left untested. Done when tests are committed with the code change.

customAnswers.customKey: 2. Verify: Author unit tests for each changed path in the source code/CI-CD repository
customAnswers.value: Inspect the PR in the source code/CI-CD repository; pass if every changed public method has a corresponding test following arrange/act/assert and no test depends on wall-clock or network.

customAnswers.customKey: 3. Run the unit test suite in GitHub Actions
customAnswers.value: The Software Engineer runs the suite on every commit locally and confirms it executes in GitHub Actions on the pull request. Done when the CI test job is green at the head commit.

customAnswers.customKey: 3. Verify: Run the unit test suite in GitHub Actions
customAnswers.value: Open the PR check in GitHub Actions; pass if the unit test job ran at the head commit SHA with all tests green.

customAnswers.customKey: 4. Evaluate the coverage gate in GitHub Actions
customAnswers.value: The Software Engineer evaluates the coverage gate in GitHub Actions: line coverage at least 80% overall, at least 90% on critical paths, and at least 80% on changed lines (enforced by the PR coverage diff), with the test count increasing alongside new public methods. Done when all three thresholds are met.

customAnswers.customKey: 4. Verify: Evaluate the coverage gate in GitHub Actions
customAnswers.value: Open the coverage report in GitHub Actions; pass if overall >=80%, critical paths >=90%, and changed-line coverage >=80%.

customAnswers.customKey: 5. Run the mutation-testing sample on critical modules
customAnswers.value: The Backend Developer runs a mutation-testing sample on the critical modules touched by the PR to confirm assertion strength. Done when the mutation results are recorded for the sampled modules.

customAnswers.customKey: 5. Verify: Run the mutation-testing sample on critical modules
customAnswers.value: Open the mutation-testing output; pass if results exist for the sampled critical modules and confirm the tests kill the sampled mutants.

customAnswers.customKey: 6. Disposition failures, shortfalls, and flaky tests
customAnswers.value: The Software Engineer keeps the merge blocked on any red test; a coverage shortfall may be waived only via an 'SDLC-Exception' ticket owned by the Engineering Manager with a 10-business-day plan to raise coverage, and flaky tests are quarantined with a 'flaky' label and a 5-business-day fix SLA. Done when the PR is green or every gap is ticketed.

customAnswers.customKey: 6. Verify: Disposition failures, shortfalls, and flaky tests
customAnswers.value: Check the PR state; pass if no PR merged with red tests or a coverage shortfall lacking an approved 'SDLC-Exception', and quarantined tests carry the 'flaky' label with SLA dates.

customAnswers.customKey: 7. Publish coverage artifacts and record Tech Lead sign-off in the source code/CI-CD repository
customAnswers.value: The Software Engineer publishes the JUnit and coverage reports as CI artifacts in GitHub Actions (retained 90 days, tagged with the commit SHA) and records the Tech Lead's review approval on the pull request in the source code/CI-CD repository. Done when the artifacts and approval exist.

customAnswers.customKey: 7. Verify: Publish coverage artifacts and record Tech Lead sign-off in the source code/CI-CD repository
customAnswers.value: Open the run artifacts in GitHub Actions and the PR in the source code/CI-CD repository; pass if the JUnit/coverage reports are attached SHA-tagged and the PR shows a Tech Lead approving review.
